summary: The change places findings on patch-less text files inline by taking their hunks from GitHub's whole diff, then from the clone. Both sources were measured against GitHub before the build, every new path was seen red first in tests/gh-test.sh, and the old placement cases are untouched. The findings sit at the edges of the new paths: the refusal handling depends on a body field and on a command substitution whose failure is never checked, a few cause lines give the wrong reason in corner cases, and some texts do not yet state every condition the code applies. The repository has no scheduled or queued work that could overlap with these files.

findings.title: Known limits does not list every case that still ends up in the review body
findings.proposedFix: Update the Known limits bullet in README.md (line 114). Say the clone is asked for any patch-less text file the whole diff does not give, on a PR of any size. Add to what stays in the body: a rename with no text changes, a comment the fallback moved after GitHub refused the review, a path git quotes in a diff header, and, on any PR, a patch-less file when the clone lacks the commits. In docs/running.md step 1, complete the parenthetical or mark it as examples.

findings.title: New temp files are left in TMPDIR when the script fails or is interrupted
findings.description:
Some temp files are removed only when their function returns normally:
- in `recover_hunks`: `wanted` (339), `whole` (347), `found` and `missing` (353-354) and `one` (363);
- in `place_comments`: `kinds` and `recovered` (419-420).
The EXIT traps name only `hunks` (531, `place`) and `hunks`, `response`, `gh_err`, `sourced`, `too_large` (701, `post-review`). Reproduced: the two failing `place` runs of R1-8 left six `redline-gh.*` files in TMPDIR (positions 72,175 B, kinds 859 B, recovered 0 B, twice). `whole` holds the whole-PR diff while it downloads (2,587,705 bytes for #94 in shape.md), so an interrupt then leaves megabytes. The base's `place_comments` already left its `positions` file untrapped, so the pattern predates this PR; the seven files above are new. The files are in TMPDIR, not the repository, so the run-record commit does not stage them. The EXIT-trap rule in agent-os/standards/scripts/bash-conventions.md:13 covers `defer`'s record written beside the repository's files, not these.
findings.proposedFix: Make each subcommand's temp files in one `mktemp -d` directory that the subcommand's EXIT trap removes, or add every file to that trap's list.

findings.title: The clone source needs GitHub's base.sha locally, and two texts promise it without that condition
findings.description:
Lines 357-362 read the PR's `base.sha` and `head.sha` from GitHub. They use the clone only when `git cat-file -e` finds both commits, then compute the merge base from them. The diff needs only the merge base, but a clone whose base branch was fetched before GitHub's `base.sha` moved gives no hunks. Every comment on a patch-less file then sits under "could not be had", which is no worse than before this PR. Redline does not fetch during a run: the precheck reads `origin/<baseRefName>` and warns when it is missing (skills/redline/SKILL.md:99).
README.md:114 states the condition ("when the clone does not hold the PR's base and head commits"). Two texts do not:
- SKILL.md:99's over-300-files warning ("the hunks of a text file whose patch GitHub omits come from this clone");
- docs/running.md:29 ("so inline anchoring still works, except in a binary file and in one whose diff GitHub takes no comment on").
The code requirement and the gap in the texts are read off the lines cited. Not measured here: whether and when GitHub moves an open PR's `base.sha` after the base branch moves, which is what makes the case common or rare.
findings.proposedFix: State the condition in SKILL.md step 7's warning and in docs/running.md's launch paragraph ("when this clone holds the PR's base and head commits"). Optionally, when `base.sha` is missing, compute the merge base from the head and the local `origin/<baseRefName>`, and let the 422 fallback catch any mismatch.

findings.title: GIT_DIFF_OPTS in the environment overrides the pinned -U3 of the clone's diff
findings.description:
The pinned `git diff` at 365-367 passes `-U3`. git's own manual on this machine (/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/share/man/man1/git.1:1657) says of GIT_DIFF_OPTS: "This takes precedence over any "-U" or "--unified" option value passed on the Git diff command line." The script neither unsets the variable nor clears the environment.
- With `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0` exported, the clone's hunks have no context lines. A comment on a context line of a patch-less file is moved under "The line is not in the pull request's diff:" even though GitHub would take it, so the stated cause is false.
- With a larger value, the hunks are wider than GitHub's. A comment beyond GitHub's three context lines is placed inline, GitHub refuses it, and the fallback moves every sourced comment into the body.
I could not run it, since the guard refuses a `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=` prefix for this role. The candidate reproduced it with git 2.54 (`@@ -20 +20 @@` in place of `@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@`). The pinned-configuration case (tests/gh-test.sh:466-467) sets only `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`.
Conditions: GIT_DIFF_OPTS is exported in the environment the GitHub agent's shell inherits from the user's profile, and the clone path is taken (a PR over 300 files, a refused whole diff, or a file the whole diff lacks). The PR's promise is that "a git configuration cannot move a hunk". An environment variable is not configuration in git's terms, but the standard's stated intent is that the user's git setup cannot move a hunk.
findings.proposedFix: Run the pinned diff as `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS git --literal-pathspecs ...`. Add a case beside the pinned-configuration one in tests/gh-test.sh that exports `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0` and expects the same placement (`[[1500,98,1300],["R1-3","R1-5"]]`).

findings.title: A mode-only change or a removed empty file may be labelled binary
findings.description:
Line 429 gives the kind `binary` to every listing entry with `patch` null, `changes` 0 and a status other than renamed. Its comments are then posted under "The file is binary and has no hunks:". If GitHub's listing shows a mode-only change (`chmod +x` on a script) or a removed empty file that way, the stated cause is false for a text file. shape.md decision 24 records the added empty file as a known edge; the mode-only and removed-empty cases are not recorded.
What I tried:
- `git log --summary` on origin/main shows no "mode change" in this repository's history, so no merged PR here shows GitHub's listing for one;
- the gh-test fixtures and the #111 measurement have no such file.
The claim turns on what GitHub's files listing returns for these two cases.
findings.proposedFix: Label that kind "The file has no text hunks (binary, a mode change or an empty file):", or record the mode-only and removed-empty cases beside decision 24 in shape.md.
findings.wouldConfirm: The files listing of a PR whose only change to a text file is `chmod +x`, and of one that removes an empty file, read for whether `patch` is absent and `changes` is 0.

findings.title: After the fallback, an off-hunk comment is listed as one GitHub refused inline
findings.description:
Line 728 sets `listing_only=1` after any 422 other than too-large on a review with a sourced comment. In that pass, line 431 gives every file whose hunks came from a source the kind `refused`, and `cause` (447) passes it through. Every comment on such a file therefore lands under "GitHub refused a review that placed these inline (<message>), so they are here:" (440).
A comment that was off those recovered hunks was moved under the offhunk line in the first pass and never sent, because `placed` (446) requires its key in the positions. The second review's line therefore says something false about it.
Traced with the fixture's src/big.js (hunks at 100 and 1001-2500):
1. Pass 1 sends a comment at :1500 and moves one at :500 as offhunk.
2. A 422 `Line could not be resolved` arrives.
3. Pass 2 lists both under the refused line.
The fallback case at tests/gh-test.sh:530 has only comments that were inline. Conditions: the fallback path runs, and the same review has an off-hunk comment on a sourced file.
Two readings:
(a) a comment the first pass found off the hunks keeps the offhunk line, since that is why it was never inline;
(b) the refused line is reworded so it does not claim that every comment under it was placed inline, since GitHub's refusal puts the recovered hunks in doubt.
Either way, the line as written is false for that comment.
findings.proposedFix: In listing-only mode, give `refused` only to a comment whose key is in the positions, and keep `offhunk` for the rest (or reword the refused line). Add a case beside tests/gh-test.sh:526-532 with a comment at src/big.js:500 that expects it under the offhunk line in the second review.

findings.title: A finding with no file is listed under "The file is not in this pull request"
findings.description:
When the reviewer leaves a coverage candidate with no file unaccounted for, the workflow mints it with the placeholder path `(no file)` (workflows/redline-loop.js:1823, 1940). It posts that path as the comment's `path` (2917). The path is in no listing, so `cause` (447) gives `absent`. The body then lists the finding under "The file is not in this pull request:" with the path line `(no file):12`.
Reproduced: `redline-gh.sh place 112 /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-nofile.json` printed exactly that grouping and moved it with path `(no file)`. Before this PR the finding sat under "Not placed inline" with no reason line; the new line names a cause that is not the real one. The placeholder is outside the diff (the workflow); the cause line is in it.
findings.proposedFix: Give a comment whose path is `(no file)` its own line ("The finding names no file:"), or have the workflow leave such findings out of `comments` and list them in the body itself.

findings.title: A comment with no path now crashes place, where the base moved it into the body
findings.description:
`placed` (446) and `cause` (447) index the kinds object with `.path`. A comment with no `path` makes jq fail with "Cannot index object with null", and the `//` alternative does not absorb the error: `{"a.txt":"hunks"} | (.[null] // "absent")` exits 5.
Reproduced: `redline-gh.sh place 112 /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-nopath.json` (one comment with `line` and `body` but no `path`, one on README.md:114) printed `jq: error ... Cannot index object with null (null)`, exited non-zero and printed nothing on stdout.
The base built `key` as `.path + "\t" + ...`, which jq evaluates for a null path (`"\tRIGHT\t3"`, checked with `jq -n`). So the removed line `(.comments | map(select($ok[key] != true))) as $moved` moved such a comment into the body, and `place` exited 0. In `post-review` the same failure is silent and an empty payload is posted (R1-9).
Conditions: only a hand-written review file triggers it. The workflow always writes `path: f.file` (workflows/redline-loop.js:2917), and a finding with no file gets `(no file)` (1940).
findings.proposedFix: Use `.path // ""` in `placed` and `cause` (an empty path reads as absent). Add a `place` case with a path-less comment that exits 0 and moves it.

findings.title: post-review posts an empty body when place_comments fails
findings.description:
Line 709 runs `place_comments` inside `$(...)`. Outside POSIX mode bash runs a command substitution with `-e` off, and the script does not set `inherit_errexit`. Traced:
1. A failing jq inside `place_comments` (433-456) does not stop it.
2. Its last command, `rm -f` (457), returns 0, so the assignment succeeds and `placed` is empty.
3. Line 710's jq over an empty here-string prints nothing and exits 0.
4. Line 711 POSTs a body of one newline to the reviews endpoint.
5. When that POST is taken, line 744's `--argjson moved` gets an empty string and jq exits 2 ("invalid JSON text passed to --argjson").
The coverage pass reproduced this run against the shim: an empty POST, then exit 2. I could not run `post-review` (refused to this role) or a bash demonstration (no `$` in my commands). Not measured: what GitHub does with an empty-body POST to that endpoint (most likely a 400 and exit 1; possibly a pending review).
The base's removed line `placed="$(place_comments "$all" "$2")"` had the same unchecked substitution, so the hole predates this PR. This PR adds a new way in: R1-8's path-less comment, which the base moved into the body. It also adds two more jq passes inside `place_comments`.
findings.proposedFix: Run `place_comments` into a temp file and test its exit status, or check `placed` with `jq -e 'type == "object"'` before building the payload. On failure, exit 2 with a line naming the review file, before anything is posted.

findings.title: Both refusal paths depend on a status field in GitHub's 422 body
findings.description:
Line 715 reads the refusal's kind from the response body's `status` field. Line 716 acts on neither refusal unless that field equals "422". With no such field, `status` is "" and the loop falls through to 734-736: exit 1 after one post. The 422 bodies github.com gave the #111 measurement carry `"status": "422"`, and the shim mirrors them (tests/gh-test.sh:293), so on github.com the path works.
The failure needs a host whose error bodies lack the field (the candidate names an older GitHub Enterprise Server; not measured here). On such a host:
- a comment on a patch-less file is now placed inline from the whole diff, where the base moved it into the body and the review posted;
- a too-large or unresolved refusal now ends the round's post with exit 1.
That breaks the PR's promise that "a 422 with no such comment fails as it always did, so the new path is never why a round fails to post". gh's stderr, captured in `gh_err`, says `(HTTP 422)` whatever the body holds. Traced through 711-736; the coverage pass reproduced it against the shim (a body without `status`: exit 1 after one post; with it: exit 0 after two).
findings.proposedFix: Decide the 422 from gh's stderr (`grep -qF '(HTTP 422)' "$gh_err"`), or accept a body that has an `errors` array and no `status`. Add a shim refusal without `status` that expects two posts and exit 0 (see R1-11).

findings.title: No case covers two too-large files or a 422 body without status
findings.description: The retry loop promises one more post per too-large file, but `too-large.txt` only ever holds one path (tests/gh-test.sh:517 and 534). So nothing checks that the loop goes round twice and leaves each file under the too-large line. The shim's `refuse` always writes `status: "422"` (293), so no case covers the body shape R1-10 fails on; that half is the regression test R1-10's fix would add. Checked by reading the cases at 511-545.
findings.proposedFix: Add a case with `data/huge.json` and a second sourced file in too-large.txt that expects three posts, exit 0 and both files under the too-large line. Add one whose refusal body has no `status` field.

list.summary: A refusal is only handled when GitHub's 422 error body carries a `status` field. If the body has no such field, a review whose comment sits on a too-large file now fails to post at all, where before this change that comment went into the body and the review posted. The script reads `.status` from the response and skips both retry cases when it is empty, even though gh's own stderr always says `(HTTP 422)`. Fix: decide it is a 422 from the gh stderr file (`grep -q '(HTTP 422)'`), or accept a body with an `errors` array when `status` is missing, and add a test case with no `status` field.
list.failure_scenario: A host whose error bodies have no `status` field (for example an older GitHub Enterprise Server). A comment on a patch-less file now gets hunks from the whole diff and is placed inline. GitHub answers {"message":"Unprocessable Entity","errors":["Diff entry src/x.js diff is too large"]}. `status` is "", so the script exits 1 after one post and the run stops at the post stage. Reproduced: exit=1, one post; the same body with "status":"422" gives exit 0 after two posts.

list.summary: When `place_comments` fails, `post-review` still sends a review with an empty request body. `place_comments` runs inside `$(...)`, where bash clears `set -e`, and its last command (`rm -f`) succeeds, so a failing jq inside it leaves `placed` empty with status 0. The script then builds an empty payload, POSTs it, and fails later on `--argjson moved` with a confusing message. Fix: check that `placed` is non-empty JSON (or run `place_comments` into a temp file and test its status) before posting.
list.failure_scenario: Any jq failure inside `place_comments` (see the missing-path entry below) or a malformed `$3`/`$4`. Reproduced: the POST goes out with an empty body, then the script prints "jq: invalid JSON text passed to --argjson" and exits 2. On GitHub an empty POST to the reviews endpoint may also create a pending review that later posts then trip over.

list.summary: After the fallback, the review body can give the wrong reason for a comment. In listing-only mode every comment on a sourced file gets the kind `refused`, including comments that were off-hunk and never placed inline. Those then appear under "GitHub refused a review that placed these inline (...)" instead of "The line is not in the pull request's diff". Fix: compute the reason as `offhunk` when the comment's key is not in the positions, and use `refused` only for comments that were actually placed.
list.failure_scenario: A review has R1-1 on a recovered hunk line and R1-2 on line 45 of the same file, outside its hunks. GitHub answers 422 "Line could not be resolved". The second post lists R1-2 under "GitHub refused a review that placed these inline (Line could not be resolved)", though the first post had already moved it to the body as off-hunk. Reproduced.

list.summary: The local-clone fallback only works if this clone holds GitHub's current `base.sha`, not just the merge base. Redline never fetches during a run, so once the base branch moves past the last local fetch, every patch-less file on a PR over 300 files falls back to "could not be had". SKILL.md step 7's warning and the launch paragraph in `docs/running.md` still say the hunks "come from this clone" and that "inline anchoring still works", with no condition. Fix: when `base.sha` is missing, find the merge base another way (fetch that one sha, or use a base-branch ref the clone has, and let the 422 fallback catch any mismatch). At minimum, state the condition in those two texts as the README does.
list.failure_scenario: A 336-file PR whose base branch got new merges after the user's last `git fetch`. `git cat-file -e <base.sha>` fails, so none of the patch-less files' findings get a thread, while the precheck warning told the person their hunks come from the clone.

list.summary: One setting in the user's environment can still change the clone's hunks. Git lets the `GIT_DIFF_OPTS` environment variable override `-U`, so `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0` drops every context line even with `-U3` pinned. Context-line findings then go into the body as "not in the pull request's diff" without a thread. Fix: run that `git diff` with `GIT_DIFF_OPTS` unset (`env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS git ...`), and add it to the pinned-configuration test case.
list.failure_scenario: With `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0` exported, the pinned command prints `@@ -20 +20 @@` instead of `@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@` (reproduced with git 2.54). A comment on a context line of a patch-less file on a PR over 300 files is moved instead of placed.

list.summary: A review comment with no `path` now crashes `place`, where before it was moved into the body. The new `$kind[.path]` lookup fails with "Cannot index object with null", and in `post-review` the empty-body problem above hides the failure. Redline's own review files always carry a path (the findings schema requires `file`), so this only affects hand-written review files. Fix: use `$kind[.path // ""]` in `placed` and `cause`, as the old `key` handled a null path.
list.failure_scenario: A review file with {line: 3, body: "**R1-1** ..."} and no path: the old `place` exits 0 and moves R1-1 into the body. The new `place` exits 5 with the jq error, and the new `post-review` sends an empty payload and exits 2. Reproduced.

list.summary: The README's Known limits line is supposed to list what still ends up in the review body (spec decision 5), but it leaves several cases out. Missing: a rename with no text changes (it has its own reason line), the 422 fallback that moves every comment on a recovered file into the body, paths git always quotes (a quote, a backslash, a tab or a newline) on a PR of any size, and a PR of 300 files or fewer where the whole diff is refused and the clone lacks the commits. It also says the clone is used only "on a PR over 300 files", but deviation 20 also uses it on smaller PRs. Step 1 of `docs/running.md` (line 37) likewise leaves out "could not be had" and the fallback. Fix: complete both lists.
list.failure_scenario: A finding on `lib/a"b.txt`, or one moved by the fallback after a 422, ends up in the body although the README's list says only binary, too-large, off-hunk, not-in-PR and over-300-without-commits findings do. A teammate reading Known limits cannot tell why.

list.summary: The script assumes `patch` null with `changes` 0 means a binary file, so a comment on a mode-only change (such as `chmod +x` on a script) or on a removed empty file is listed under "The file is binary and has no hunks". The added empty file is already recorded as a known edge in `shape.md` decision 24; these two cases are not. Fix: label this "has no text hunks", or add the mode-only and removed-empty cases to decision 24's record.
list.failure_scenario: A PR makes `scripts/deploy.sh` executable with no content change, so the listing has patch null and changes 0. A finding at `scripts/deploy.sh:1` is posted under "The file is binary and has no hunks:".

list.summary: Some temp files are left behind when the script fails or is interrupted. The files `recover_hunks` makes (`wanted`, `whole`, `found`, `missing`, `one`) and the new `kinds` and `recovered` files in `place_comments` are not in any EXIT trap. `whole` holds the whole-PR diff, which was 2.6 MB on #94. The `defer` subcommand already removes its temp files on every way out (#97, R1-3). Fix: register these files with the subcommand's EXIT trap, or make them inside one temp directory the trap removes.
list.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C while `gh api ... -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.diff'` is downloading, or a `set -e` exit in `wanted_files` on a malformed review file: the redline-gh.XXXXXX files stay in TMPDIR, megabytes each for a large PR.

list.summary: The retry loop's main promise, one more post per too-large file, is only tested with one too-large file. Nothing tests two such files in one review (where the loop has to go round twice), and nothing tests a 422 body without `status`. Fix: add a case with two paths in `too-large.txt` that expects three posts and exit 0, and a refusal case whose body has no `status` field.
list.failure_scenario: A change that adds only the first named file and then falls through to the listing-only branch, or the `status` dependency in the first entry, would pass all 237 cases.

list.summary: A finding with no file gets a misleading reason in the review body. The workflow gives such coverage findings the placeholder path `(no file)` (`NO_FILE` in `workflows/redline-loop.js`), so `place_comments` lists them under "The file is not in this pull request:" with a path line of `(no file):<line>`. Fix: give comments whose path is `(no file)` their own reason line, such as "The finding names no file:", or have the workflow leave them out of `comments`.
list.failure_scenario: The reviewer does not account for a coverage candidate that has no file. It becomes an unconfirmed finding with path "(no file)" and is posted under "The file is not in this pull request:" as `(no file):12`.
